exact_derivation: At u=1/2 the smooth step has beta=1/2, beta'=2, beta''=0, beta'''=-16. For example beta(u)=1/(1+exp(1/u-1/(1-u))) for 0<u<1; the Taylor expansion at 1/2 yields these derivatives.
The slot argument has derivative 3/(s1-s0)=15N, so theta'''(z_r)=beta'''(1/2)(15N)^3=-54000 N^3.
Therefore c''(z_r)=theta'''(z_r) log(B^-1)=54000 N^3 log B>0.
The full spatial Laplacian of the local three-dimensional W is Delta W=(c''(Z)(X-pi_1),-c''(Z)(Y-pi_2),0). Hence Delta W(Q_r)=(13500 lambda N^3 log(B)/B,0,0), which is nonzero.
For t>=1, alpha_1(t)=1/(1+t), alpha_1'(t)=-(1+t)^-2, and the raw force is f_raw(t)=-(1+t)^-2 W+(1+t)^-2 A(W)-nu(1+t)^-1 Delta W, where A(W)=(W·grad)W.

W is divergence-free and spatially mean-zero on the torus; Delta W is likewise divergence-free and mean-zero. The Leray projection therefore satisfies P W=W and P Delta W=Delta W. Consequently f_projected(t)=P f_raw(t)=-(nu/(1+t)) Delta W+(P A(W)-W)/(1+t)^2.
For every integer h>=0, (1+t)^(1+h) partial_t^h f_projected(t,x) tends pointwise (indeed in each finite C^r norm for fixed smooth W) to (-1)^(h+1) nu h! Delta W(x), as t tends to infinity.

At Q_r the first coordinate of this limit is (-1)^(h+1) nu h! 13500 lambda N^3 log(B)/B, nonzero. Therefore no global C^r upper bound O((1+t)^(-1-h-delta)) with delta>0 can hold for the projected force, for any r>=0. The October common exponent 1+h is sharp for this actual construction when nu>0.

With Delta phi_W=div A(W), mean(phi_W)=0, the projected mean-zero pressure is p_projected(t)=-(1+t)^-2 phi_W. The earlier protected positive divergence witness at q_r shows phi_W is nonzero. Hence its C^r decay exponent 2+h is also sharp for every h,r>=0; this is stronger than the common 1+h envelope asserted in the manuscript.
theorem: For the actual source-defined row-2 scaling branch and every fixed nu>0, projected force has nonzero asymptotic (1+t)^(1+h) partial_t^h P f_alpha1 -> (-1)^(h+1) nu h! Delta W; at Q_r the leading coefficient has absolute value nu h! 13500 lambda N^3 log(B)/B. Thus the manuscript's (1+t)^(-1-h) projected-force bound cannot be improved to any strictly faster uniform power. The projected pressure instead has exact (1+t)^(-2-h) rate and nonzero spatial profile.
